In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is empirical evidence supporting that authoring tools can be beneficial for non-programmer ITS authors.
ITS authoring tools can be used to support non-programmer authors in designing different types of ITS, and that the design of authoring tools can also be used to improve ITS authoring process.
the ITS community has been successfully using ITS authoring tool to design ITS, but still there are several opportunities for further research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ITS authoring tools have a great potential to facilitate ITS design for nonprogrammer authors and, consequently, to increase the number of ITS available for students.

there is a great diversity of authoring tools, with different features and technologies used to develop them, and that they have been mainly used for authoring learning content and tutors, specially before the instruction.
ITS authoring tools are a valuable resource to design ITS, but there are still several open issues that need to be addressed.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is empirical evidence on the benefits of using ITS authorings tools for non-programmers, but more research is still necessary to further improve authoring tools, specially by providing better support for authoring pedagogical and domain models.
there is a need for a better understanding of the benefits and challenges of using authoring tools to design ITS for non-programmer users.
there is still a need of further empirical research to understand and improve how authoring tools support the design of ITS by non-programmer developers.
